correctness.rationale: By the complete three-value Łukasiewicz strong-conjunction table, only 1-1 and mixed 1-half paths have nonzero strength. The threshold supports consequently satisfy precisely \(P\circ P\subseteq P\), \(P\circ H\subseteq H\), and \(H\circ P\subseteq H\), with a reverse construction. Collapse of P-equivalence classes makes H constant on pairs of blocks; its excess over the quotient order is exactly an upset of the induced complement in \(Q^{\mathrm{op}}\times Q\). This is bijective. Stirling counting and the staircase/Dyck-path correspondence establish all n and Catalan claims. An independently written standalone exhaustive matrix checker has verified all \(3^{n(n-1)}\) cases for \(1\le n\le4\), while poset enumeration independently verifies \(T_1,\ldots,T_4\) and the Catalan specialization through seven classes. Finite experiments are not being promoted to a general proof.

value.rationale: Finite three-grade Łukasiewicz accessibility is the smallest non-Boolean subclass of a recently developed Kripke/topological semantic framework. The result supplies a complete uniform structural classification and exact all-n enumerator with an independently meaningful Catalan boundary (total-preorder crisp cores), not merely a one-size numerical increment. It also separates non-idempotent Łukasiewicz half-edge behavior from max–min fuzzy preorders, clarifying which constraints genuinely survive thresholding. Arbitrary-size asymptotics or downstream applications are not claimed.
